case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.court: Supreme Court of the United States
key_cases.holding: The Court held that the Adoption Assistance and Child Welfare Act's reasonable-efforts provision, 42 U.S.C. § 671(a)(15), creates no right enforceable by beneficiaries under the Act itself or under 42 U.S.C. § 1983.
key_cases.relevance: Audit findings of misused child-welfare funds likewise yield administrative recoupment rather than beneficiary suits under Suter.
key_cases.quote: We hold that the Act does not create an enforceable right on behalf of respondents.

key_cases.case_name: Beattie v. Aiken County Department of Social Services
key_cases.holding: The court held that parents whose case was closed as unfounded may not examine the DSS case file, that 'report' covers all investigative information and the reporter's identity is never disclosable, and that FOIA requires separation and release of non-exempt material where a court is asked to conduct that review.
key_cases.relevance: It also holds that agency internal investigative files must be reviewed item by item for exempt and non-exempt content rather than withheld wholesale.
key_cases.quote: The clear language of § 20-7-650 prohibits the disclosure of the DSS case file to Appellants or to anyone else.

key_cases.case_name: Disabato v. South Carolina Ass'n of School Administrators
key_cases.holding: The court held that applying the South Carolina FOIA to a nonprofit corporation supported in part by public funds does not violate its First Amendment speech and association rights, and reversed dismissal of the FOIA action.
key_cases.relevance: Contractors and associations spending public child-welfare dollars cannot avoid records requests by invoking their private form or advocacy role.
key_cases.quote: We conclude that while the FOIA does impact upon SCASA's speech and association rights, the First Amendment is not violated.

key_cases.case_name: Newberry Publishing Co. v. Newberry County Commission on Alcohol & Drug Abuse
key_cases.holding: The court reversed, holding that no criminal investigative report is per se exempt under the South Carolina FOIA and that a public body must separate exempt from non-exempt material and release the non-exempt portion, with exemption decided on a case-by-case basis.
key_cases.relevance: Newberry is the source of the rule Beattie applies: an agency holding an audit or investigative file must review it item by item and release whatever is not exempt, rather than withholding the file wholesale.
key_cases.quote: a public record containing both nonexempt and exempt material must be segregated so that the nonexempt material is made available to the public
